title: Cornelia Funke
summary: Join Cornelia Funke and Kellie Parker as they discuss the importance of physical writing, the magic of quill and ink, and the significance of respecting the land. Learn about successful nature rehabilitation at mine sites and the deep passion for protecting nature.
body_markdown:
##### Season 2: Episode 7


### Cornelia Funke on plastic pens, storytelling and sustainability


Global bestselling author Cornelia Funke (Dragon Rider, Inkheart) says she has hungry hands and that she cannot live without her pen to conjure up her magical worlds. Cornelia tells Dr Anna about the importance of the physical process of writing and illustrating, before committing her work to a computer. She also shares her deep passion for the protection of nature and our knowledge of it.


They are joined by Rio Tinto’s Chief Executive Australia, Kellie Parker, to talk about the importance of rehabilitating nature at mine sites and the ways they are being successfully rejuvenated around the world. Listen to hear about going back to quill and ink, butterfly rehabilitation, and the importance of respecting land which we use for vital materials.


Listen to the episode on[Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/episode/0XBPBEztojDheyLelJ5Rbj) ,[Apple](https://podcasts.apple.com/gb/podcast/cornelia-funke-on-plastic-pens-storytelling-and/id1732003388?i=1000706635761) ,[Amazon](https://music.amazon.com/podcasts/4fde7fdd-564a-401b-8071-58672ca0b330/episodes/4f7e809d-cd3a-471a-bf4d-c8a9eb0101b0/things-you-can't-live-without-cornelia-funke-on-plastic-pens-storytelling-and-sustainability) and[YouTube](https://youtu.be/SM_s4uCUGmI) .
